If you are looking for natural skincare in the UK with roots in Indian beauty traditions, two names come up again and again: Deyga and Vilvah. Both are Indian brands, both work with plant-based and kitchen-cupboard ingredients, and Swansura is an official UK partner of both, so every product is genuine and ships from the UK. They are not the same, though. Here is how to tell which one suits your skin, and where to start. For the ingredients behind both, read our Indian skincare guide.

The short answer

Choose Vilvah if you like creamy, comforting textures built around goat milk, oat milk and gentle botanicals. Choose Deyga if you prefer farm-grown herbs, clays, charcoal and fruit actives with a fresher feel. Many people end up using both: a Vilvah cleanser or serum in the morning and a Deyga treat, such as a lip balm or face pack, alongside it.

Vilvah: goat milk and botanical care

Vilvah is known for milk-based formulas for face, hair and body. The best place to start is Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum, a lightweight milk serum with natural milk proteins that sinks in quickly and leaves skin feeling soft rather than greasy. It is the product people search for most: "Vilvah Milk Drops" is one of the brand's top searches in the UK.

For hair, the Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo pairs goat milk with pea protein and jasmine. It is pH-balanced and free from artificial colours and fragrances, so it suits frequent washing, and it is a good fit for dry or frizzy hair. If you want the full ritual, the Goat Milk Hair Kit puts the shampoo with its partners in one box. Our natural shampoo guide compares more options.

For the body, Vilvah Milk Body Lotion uses oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane in a quick-absorbing, vegan formula that is gentle enough for the whole family. Prefer a no-scent wash? The Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is the calmest place to begin. See the whole range on our goat milk edit.

Deyga: farm-grown botanicals

Deyga makes natural skin, hair and body care with plant-based ingredients, many grown on its own farm in India. Its cult favourite is the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm: beetroot extract and natural butters give a soft, sheer tint, and the 10 g tin fits any pocket. "Deyga lip balm" is one of the brand's most searched products, and it makes an easy first try at under £11.

For oilier or combination skin, the Deyga Charcoal Face Wash uses activated charcoal for a deep, refreshing cleanse without a tight finish. For glow, the Deyga Rose Glow Serum is a light rose and saffron oil serum that leaves skin looking radiant. On wash day, Deyga Rice Water Shampoo is a gentle, sulfate-free everyday cleanser.

Which is better for your skin type?

Dry or sensitive skin

Lean towards Vilvah. Milk textures, fragrance-free options and the oat milk body lotion are made for comfort. Add a Deyga body butter for dry skin, such as the Chocolate Body Butter, for extra richness on elbows and legs.

Oily or combination skin

Start with Deyga's charcoal face wash and a lightweight serum, then use a Vilvah milk product only where skin feels dry. Our face wash for oily skin page compares the options side by side, and our guide to face wash for your skin type explains how to choose.

Dull-looking skin

Try one serum from each brand on alternate days: Vilvah Milk Drops for hydration and Deyga Rose Glow for radiance. Keep everything else simple.

A simple routine using both brands

  1. Cleanse: Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (oilier skin) or Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (drier skin).
  2. Treat: Vilvah Milk Drops in the morning, Deyga Rose Glow in the evening.
  3. Lips and body: Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm through the day and Vilvah Milk Body Lotion after showering.

Patch test anything new and introduce one product at a time. Ready-made pairings with 5% off are on our routines page.

Why buy Deyga and Vilvah from Swansura?

We are an official UK partner of both brands, so there are no grey imports and no long waits from abroad: orders are dispatched from the UK, usually within 1–2 working days, with free UK delivery over £40. Explore the full natural skincare edit, or go straight to all Deyga and all Vilvah products.

Cold wind, central heating and hot drinks all leave lips dry in winter, and a good lip balm is the simplest fix. But balms are not all the same: some carry an SPF, some add a sheer tint, and some are just a few plant oils, butters and wax. Here is how to choose a lip balm for dry lips, what is inside each type and how to get the most from it.

What a lip balm does

Lips have a very thin outer layer and no oil glands of their own, so they dry out faster than the rest of the face. A balm puts a soft layer of oils, butters and wax over them, which keeps them feeling comfortable for longer. Most balms are built from the same few things: plant oils such as almond, avocado or jojoba; butters such as shea, mango or kokum; and a wax, often beeswax, that holds it all together.

SPF lip balm

Lips burn too, on bright winter days, ski trips and holidays as much as in summer. Vilvah Milk Lip Balm SPF 30 PA+++ (£9.99) uses mineral filters, zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, in a base of coconut oil, shea butter, soy butter, kokum butter and soy milk extract, with a soft vanilla note. Apply it before going outside, and reapply often, especially after eating, drinking or swimming. It works on its own or under lipstick.

Tinted lip balm

A tinted lip balm adds a sheer wash of colour as well as moisture, so it can stand in for a lipstick on busy days.

  • Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm Classic (from £10.99, 10g pot) takes its rosy tint from beetroot extract, in almond, avocado and jojoba oils with shea butter and beeswax. The same balm comes as a twist-up Beetroot Lip Balm Stick (from £13.99, 5.5g) for your pocket.
  • Vilvah Rose Milk Lip Balm (£9.99) gives a soft pink tint, with paneer rose extract, olive squalane, avocado butter, shea butter and vitamin E.
  • Vilvah Mango Shake Lip Balm (£9.99) leaves a reddish-orange tint, with Alphonso mango pulp extract, mango butter, coconut milk and olive squalane.
  • Vilvah Filter Kaapi Lip Balm (£9.99) has a subtle brown tint inspired by South Indian filter coffee, with coffee oil, coffee extract, shea butter, coconut milk and almond oil.
  • Vilvah Grape Fruit Lip Balm (£6.99) has just six ingredients, with a little red iron oxide for a sheer tint and grapefruit essential oil for a zesty scent.

Can't choose? The Vilvah Tinted Lip Balm Kit (£17) puts two tinted balms in one box.

Natural lip balm with a short ingredient list

If you prefer a plain balm with nothing extra, look for a short list of oils, butter and wax.

  • Deyga Shea Butter Lip Balm (£9.99, 8g): almond oil, jojoba oil, beeswax, shea butter, vanilla extract and vitamin E, in a vanilla or shea version.
  • Vilvah Natural Lemon Lip Balm (£6.99): organic shea butter, avocado oil, almond oil, unrefined beeswax and lemon essential oil.

For a rich, jar-style lip butter, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50, 15ml, or a 50ml jar) is made with organic palm oil certified by the RSPO.

How to use a lip balm

  1. Start with clean, dry lips.
  2. Apply a thin layer with the stick or a clean fingertip, and reapply whenever lips feel dry.
  3. At night, use a thicker layer so it can sit on your lips while you sleep.
  4. Once or twice a week, use a lip scrub first. A balm spreads more evenly on smooth lips; our lip scrub guide explains how.
  5. In the sun, choose an SPF balm and reapply often.

Good to know

  • Try not to lick your lips: saliva dries quickly and leaves them drier than before.
  • Many balms contain beeswax. If you avoid it, check the Ingredients tab on each product before you buy.
  • Patch test balms with essential oils, such as the lemon and grapefruit balms, before first use.
  • Cracked or sore lips that do not settle after a week or two are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.
  • Lip balms make easy stocking fillers: see our stocking fillers guide.

Shop every lip balm and lip care product and our lip scrubs, all dispatched from the UK with free UK delivery over £40.

Indian skincare grows out of ingredients found in Indian kitchens and gardens: turmeric, neem, saffron, rose water, amla and coconut oil. Many people in the UK grew up with them through family routines, and many more are discovering them now. This guide explains the key ingredients, shows which products from Vilvah and Deyga actually contain them (checked against each full ingredient list), and covers how to buy Indian skincare in the UK without waiting for a parcel from India.

What makes Indian skincare different?

Two things stand out. First, the ingredients: many come from Ayurveda, India’s traditional system of wellbeing, and from everyday cooking, so the labels read like a spice rack. Deyga even lists many ingredients with their Sanskrit names, such as Haridra for turmeric, Nimba for neem, Kumkuma for saffron and Satapatrika for rose. Second, the formats: powder face packs you mix with water, oils massaged into the scalp before washing, and handmade bars. These are cosmetic products, not Ayurvedic medicines, and we describe them that way.

The key ingredients, and where to find them

Turmeric (haldi)

Turmeric is part of the Indian haldi ceremony before a wedding, when a turmeric paste is spread on the bride and groom. You will find it in the Deyga Neem & Turmeric Bath Bar (£14.99), made with coconut oil, neem hydrosol, turmeric and shea butter, and in the Deyga Orange & Almond Face Pack (£19.99), a three-ingredient powder of sun-dried orange pulp and zest, almond meal and turmeric. Turmeric can colour towels and nails, so rinse well.

Neem

Neem is a tree grown across India, and its leaves and seeds are used in hair and skin care. Deyga Neem Seed Oil (£14.99) has one ingredient: neem seed oil, with a strong, earthy scent. The Deyga Spirulina Matcha Face Pack (£17.99) mixes neem leaf with spirulina, matcha, moringa and aloe vera powder.

Saffron (kesar or kumkuma)

Saffron is one of the most prized spices in Indian cooking and a long-standing beauty ingredient. The Deyga Rose Glow Serum (£17.99) is a face oil of native rose and saffron in virgin coconut, pomegranate seed, rosehip, almond and jojoba oils. The Deyga Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99) pairs saffron with raw shea butter, and the Vilvah Milk Mud Mask (£19.99) combines kaolin clay, licorice root, oat milk and saffron extract.

Rose water (gulab jal)

Rose water is a staple of Indian dressing tables, used to refresh the face or mix face packs. Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99) has two ingredients: rose and distilled water. It is also the classic liquid for mixing a powder face pack.

Clay and multani mitti

Multani mitti, or fuller’s earth, is the traditional Indian clay for face packs. Our clay products use kaolin and French pink clay instead, such as the Milk Mud Mask above. Our face mask guide explains how to use clay masks and powder packs.

Amla, bhringraj and hibiscus for hair

Oiling the hair before washing is one of the best-known Indian routines. Deyga’s Hair Growth Oil (£14.99) is a coconut, almond and castor oil base with amla, bhringraj, hibiscus, fenugreek, curry leaves and vetiver: a classic Indian herbal hair oil. Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99) is a lighter, leave-in option with black seed oil, curry leaf oil, hibiscus oil and amla extract, and Vilvah Herbal Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) includes neem leaf, amla and basil leaf water. Read our hair oil guide for how to oil your hair.

Beetroot and goat milk

Two newer favourites: the Deyga Beetroot Lip Balm (from £10.99) is made with beetroot extract, almond, avocado and jojoba oils and shea butter, and Vilvah builds much of its range on goat milk (see our goat milk soap guide).

A simple way to start

  1. Cleanse: a handmade bar such as the Neem & Turmeric bar for the body, or a gentle face wash.
  2. Refresh: pat on rose water with clean hands or a cotton pad.
  3. Nourish: a few drops of a face oil such as the Rose Glow Serum in the evening.
  4. Once a week: a powder face pack mixed with rose water, or a clay mask.
  5. Hair: oil the scalp and lengths an hour or more before washing, then shampoo.

Many of these products contain essential oils or strongly scented plant ingredients, so patch test anything you leave on the skin, and keep powders and oils away from the eyes. For which brand suits your skin type, read Deyga or Vilvah; for adding a serum, see our face serum guide.

Buying Indian skincare in the UK

  • Official UK partner: Swansura is an official UK partner of both Deyga and Vilvah, so every product is genuine.
  • Shipped from the UK: orders leave our UK stock, so there is no wait for a parcel from India and no import charge at your door.
  • Full ingredient lists: almost every product page has the full ingredient list on its Ingredients tab, so you can check before you buy.
  • Delivery: UK delivery is free on orders over £40, and unopened items can be returned within 14 days.

Browse all our natural skincare, or shop by brand: Vilvah and Deyga.

A face serum is a light, concentrated step that sits between cleansing and moisturising. Most are watery or gel-like and carry one or two key ingredients, such as vitamin C, hyaluronic acid or niacinamide. Here is what each of those ingredients is, how to choose a serum, and how to layer it.

Serum, moisturiser or face oil?

  • Water-based serums are thin and quick to absorb. They go on first, after cleansing and toning.
  • Moisturisers are creams or lotions that hold moisture in. They go on after your serum.
  • Oil serums are blends of plant oils. They can be used last at night, or mixed with a drop of moisturiser.

Vitamin C serum

Vitamin C is an antioxidant, and one of the most searched serum ingredients. Pure vitamin C (ascorbic acid) can be unstable, so many serums use a gentler, more stable form. Deyga 10% Vitamin C Face Serum (from £16.99, 20ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with orange and citrus extracts. Use a vitamin C serum in the morning, and always finish with sunscreen. See every vitamin C serum.

Hyaluronic acid serum

Hyaluronic acid is a moisture-loving ingredient that holds water in the skin, so it suits every skin type, including oily skin. Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) combines sodium hyaluronate with glycerine, panthenol, aloe vera and centella asiatica, and is made without fragrance. Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum (from £21.99) pairs aloe vera juice and hyaluronic acid with rice milk extract and alpha arbutin. Apply either to slightly damp skin.

Niacinamide, bakuchiol and ceramides

Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 that is easy to pair with other ingredients. If you are looking for a niacinamide serum, read the full ingredient list: niacinamide often works alongside other ingredients rather than on its own. Bakuchiol is a plant extract often used as a gentle alternative to retinol, and ceramides are lipids that are naturally found in skin. Vilvah Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml) brings all three together, with hyaluronic acid, olive squalane, blue pea flower extract and a plant peptide extract. The Vilvah AM PM Serum Kit (£47.99) pairs it with Milk Drops: Milk Drops in the morning, Better Ageing at night. For dry, mature skin, Highborn London MOISTUREBURST Serum (from £57) is a ceramide serum made to layer under moisturiser.

Face oil serums

Oil serums suit dry skin and evening routines. Deyga Rose Glow Serum (£17.99, 30ml) blends rose and saffron with coconut, pomegranate seed, rosehip, almond and jojoba oils. Deyga Beautifying Serum (from £17.99, 30ml) uses moringa, kukui, grapeseed and vetiver oils. Warm two or three drops between your palms and press them into the skin.

How to choose a face serum

Serum, moisturiser or face oil?

  • Water-based serums are thin and quick to absorb. They go on first, after cleansing and toning.

Vitamin C is an antioxidant, and one of the most searched serum ingredients. Pure vitamin C (ascorbic acid) can be unstable, so many serums use a gentler, more stable form. Goat milk soap is a bar soap made with goat milk in its recipe. It gives a creamy lather and leaves skin feeling soft rather than tight, which is why many people keep a bar by the bath or basin. This guide explains how goat milk soap is made, how to use it on your face and body, and how to choose between the goat milk soaps from Vilvah, one of the two Indian natural brands Swansura is an official UK partner of.

What is goat milk soap?

Every true bar soap is made by mixing oils or butters with lye (sodium hydroxide). The two react together to form soap, a process called saponification. In goat milk soap, fresh goat milk goes into the recipe, which gives the bar a creamy lather. You will see sodium hydroxide at the end of the ingredient lists below: that is how all bar soap is made.

Vilvah makes its goat milk bars by hand with farm-fresh goat milk and a base of plant oils such as extra virgin olive, coconut and castor oil. Coconut oil gives the bubbly lather, olive oil a gentle feel and castor oil a cushioned foam.

The Vilvah goat milk soaps

  • Classic Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): goat milk, olive, coconut and castor oils, lightly scented with lavender essential oil. Six ingredients in all, and listed as suiting dry and sensitive skin.
  • Classic Rose Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 125g): goat milk with rose petals, rose hydrosol, French pink clay, shea butter and rice bran oil, scented with rose and geranium essential oils.
  • Charcoal Goat Milk Soap (£9.99, 115g): activated charcoal with goat milk, for a clean-feeling daily wash. The charcoal gives the bar its colour.

All three are in our goat milk soap collection. One bar that looks similar is not a goat milk soap: Vilvah’s Cucumber, Curd & Mint Soap (£9.99) is made with cucumber juice, curd and mint leaves, for a cool, zesty morning wash.

Which bar should you choose?

  • A soft, simple scent: the Classic bar, with lavender.
  • A floral scent: Classic Rose.
  • A clean-feeling wash: Charcoal.
  • Something fresh and minty: Cucumber, Curd & Mint.
  • A bar without milk: Deyga’s Shea Saffron Bath Bar (£15.99) and Rose Pink Clay Bath Bar (£14.99) are made with raw shea butter and coconut and olive oils. Our body wash and bath bar guide compares them with Deyga’s other bars and body washes.

How to use goat milk soap

  1. Wet your skin and the bar, then work up a lather between your hands.
  2. Massage the foam over damp face or body, keeping it away from your eyes.
  3. Rinse well with warm water and pat dry.
  4. Follow with a moisturiser or body lotion if your skin tends to feel dry.
  5. Keep the bar on a draining soap dish between uses. A handmade bar left sitting in water softens quickly.

The Classic, Classic Rose and Cucumber bars contain essential oils, so patch test before first use.

Goat milk shampoo and hair care

Goat milk is not only for soap. Vilvah Goat Milk Shampoo (£15.99, 250ml) is a creamy shampoo with goat milk, jasmine flower water and hydrolysed pea protein, with a light jasmine and citrus scent. Vilvah Goat Milk Hair Mask (£31.99) pairs goat milk with ceramides and argan oil to condition dry, frizzy lengths. Buy them together in the Goat Milk Hair Kit (£34.99), or try the shampoo with Vilvah’s Cream Conditioner in the Bestseller Hair Kit (£27.99). Our natural shampoo guide covers how to choose a shampoo for dry hair.

Goat milk for the body

The Vilvah Milk Body Kit (£44.99) pairs a Goat Milk Body Wash, made with goat milk, chamomile water and coconut oil and scented with vanilla, with a Milk Body Lotion. If you were looking for a goat milk body lotion, note that the Milk Body Lotion (£25.99) is made with oat milk, ceramide NP and olive squalane: the goat milk in this kit is in the body wash. For richer body care after a soap, read our body butter guide.

Good to know

  • Goat milk soap is not vegan, because it contains goat milk.
  • Every skin is different. If you have a skin condition, ask a pharmacist or GP before trying a new soap.
  • A goat milk bar wrapped in tissue makes an easy gift: see our stocking fillers and stocking fillers guide.
  • Everything is 100% authentic and shipped from the UK. Browse the whole goat milk range; UK delivery is free on orders over £40.
